newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's CPN nets PLN 133.6 mln in 13 months.
newsitem.headline: Poland's CPN nets PLN 133.6 mln in 13 months.

text.p: Poland's state-owned petrol distribution chain Centrala Produktow Naftowych SA (CPN) netted 133.6 mliion zlotys in the 13 months ending in December 1996, company spokeswoman Maria Zawislak said on Monday.
CPN decided to report results for 13 months as a separate accounting period because it was transformed into a treasury-owned joint-stock company on December 1, 1995, Zawislak told Reuters.
During 1995's first 11 months, when CPN functioned as an enterprise directly controlled by the industry ministry, the company netted 109 million zlotys, she said.
CPN's gross profit reached 264.8 million zlotys on sales of 11.1 billion zlotys in the 13-month period, compared with 197.7 million and 8.8 billion zlotys respectivly in 1995's first 11 months.
CPN, Poland's petrol distribution monopolist before the 1989 fall of communism, owns 1,374 filling stations out of Poland's 4,600.
The government plans to allot CPN's shares to state oil holding Nafta Polska SA, which has already been given control over Poland's seven refineries.
The refineries are to be partially sold off and investors are to get access to CPN's chain as an incentive.
